input.summary: Jordan Doe's (jdoe@example.com, on PTO 10/12–10/19, normally uses macOS) credentials were used from 198.51.100.23. That IP belongs to NIGHTOWL-HOSTING in the Netherlands, is known bulletproof hosting, runs an open Docker registry on port 5000 and is tagged for k8s API brute-forcing. The actor used a Linux kubectl client and ran the same playbook against all three payments-prod clusters in turn: EKS 14:02–14:25, GKE 14:38–15:01, AKS 15:11–15:34. In each cluster the actor checked their own permissions (selfsubjectrulesreviews) and listed namespaces. Their attempts to read kube-system secrets and create a kube-system job were denied. They then read payments/payments-db-credentials and created a privileged pod, payments/debug-tools-7f9c (alpine, hostPID, hostNetwork, host root mounted, not on the allowlist), and exec'd into it. Within minutes, the cluster-admin argocd-application-controller service account token was used from the same outside IP, even though that account normally runs only from inside the cluster. The pod gave host access, so the token was most likely taken from the node through it. The token was used to create a ClusterRoleBinding, 'jdoe-break-glass', that gives jdoe cluster-admin. With that access the actor set up persistence: a kube-system DaemonSet 'kube-metrics-agent' and a CronJob 'node-cert-rotate' (runs every 15 min), both pulling images from 198.51.100.23:5000, plus a NodePort service 'metrics-agent-np' on port 30080. Last, they listed secrets across all namespaces (the alert). All three clouds are affected. Recommended actions: revoke jdoe's sessions on every cloud, rotate the argocd service account tokens and all payments secrets (DB credentials first), delete the CRBs, DaemonSets, CronJobs, NodePort services and debug pods, and treat the nodes as compromised.
